- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp upward spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 3–5%.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct — adjust forecast slope downward after peak to reflect mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends; increase forecast by 2–4% in such regimes.
- Forecast exhibits persistent upward bias in high-volatility periods; apply downward correction proportional to recent volatility (e.g., 10% if 3-day std > 5).
- Model fails to capture sudden downward corrections; if true outcome drops >5% from prior day, reduce forecast by 5–10% immediately.
- Forecast often lags true price movements by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with actual momentum.
- In low-volatility periods, model tends to over-smooth; increase forecast variance by 1–2% to reflect hidden volatility.
